name: Magnetic compass for direction finding
summary: Chinese technical writers of the eleventh century described magnetized pointers, floated or hung, that give a fixed direction for finding the way.
description: A magnetized indicator supplies a directional reference, with floating and suspended implementations documented in Chinese technical accounts.
tier_reason: Magnetic direction finding supports subsequent navigation, surveying and seafaring across regions and generations.

impact.note: A new direction-finding ability that spread across many societies, on which navigation, surveying, mining and the study of magnetism rested for centuries.
